**PTZ for `bc://` cameras.** go2rtc's ONVIF server now offers pan, tilt, zoom and presets for Reolink cameras connected over
Baichuan, and turns the ONVIF calls into Baichuan PTZ messages. Frigate and Home Assistant only speak ONVIF for PTZ, so they
point at go2rtc instead of the camera, which can keep its own ONVIF and RTSP switched off.

Builds on [v1.9.15-baichuan.1](https://github.com/privatecoder/go2rtc/releases/tag/v1.9.15-baichuan.1), the first release
with the native Baichuan source.

## Highlights

- **Pan and tilt** in eight directions, with the speed taken from the ONVIF velocity.
- **Zoom**: the camera's own continuous zoom, where the lens runs until Stop or the end of its range. Cameras that refuse it,
  and moves that pan and zoom at once, get stepped zoom instead.
- **Presets**: list, go to, and save (`SetPreset` into the slot the client names or the lowest free one). `RemovePreset` is
  not supported; presets can be deleted in the Reolink app.
- **Stop is not left to chance**: a move without a Stop ends by itself after 10 seconds, or after the request's ONVIF
  `Timeout` if that is shorter. A Stop the camera does not acknowledge is sent again.
- **One login per camera**: PTZ uses the session of the camera's running stream and does not touch the video. Only when no
  stream of that camera is running does go2rtc open a session of its own, and closes it after a minute without use.
- **Nothing logs in at start**: go2rtc asks the cameras about PTZ when an ONVIF client first connects. A profile gets PTZ only
  if its camera reports pan/tilt or zoom. Offline cameras are retried with backoff and keep their other profile data.
- **The same for IP and UID cameras**, including cameras reached over P2P.

## Usage

```yaml
# Frigate config.yml
cameras:
  e1-zoom:
    onvif:
      host: 127.0.0.1         # go2rtc, here inside the Frigate container
      port: 1984              # go2rtc's API port
      profile: e1-zoom        # the go2rtc stream name
```

The user and password the client sends are ignored. Home Assistant's ONVIF integration pointed at go2rtc gets the same PTZ.
Details: [internal/bc/README.md](https://github.com/privatecoder/go2rtc/blob/v1.9.15-baichuan.2/internal/bc/README.md#ptz-frigate-home-assistant).

**Security:** go2rtc's ONVIF server ignores the ONVIF user and password. Without an API password, anyone who can reach port 1984
can move the cameras (as they can already watch them), so keep it on a trusted network. With an API password set, every path on
port 1984 including `/onvif/` needs HTTP Basic auth, except requests from `127.0.0.1`:

```yaml
go2rtc:          # in Frigate's config; plain go2rtc.yaml starts at api:
  api:
    username: someuser
    password: somepass
```

Frigate's bundled go2rtc is reached over `127.0.0.1` and keeps PTZ. ONVIF clients on other machines, such as Home Assistant's
ONVIF integration, usually don't send HTTP Basic auth and are then refused.

## Tested

- On a Reolink E1 Zoom, by IP and by UID over P2P: every direction, Stop, the safety stop, zoom to both ends, saving a preset
  and going between presets.
- Frigate's own ONVIF client (onvif-zeep-async) against go2rtc: Frigate sees pan/tilt and zoom, lists the presets, and moves,
  stops and goes to presets. From a cold start, only one camera login happened.
- Unit tests with the race detector for the PTZ controller (stop retries, deadlines, session ordering, zoom fallback) and the
  ONVIF PTZ service.

## Known limitations

- No autotracking: only continuous movement is offered, no relative or absolute moves and no position status, so Frigate shows
  autotracking as unsupported.
- A camera that refuses a PTZ feature once keeps it disabled until go2rtc restarts, and a changed stream URL is picked up for
  PTZ only after a restart.
- Not supported: motion events, SD-card playback, PTZ calibration, focus, patrols and camera settings.

## Credits

The PTZ message layouts (PTZ control, presets, zoom and focus) come from upstream **neolink** by George Hilliard
(thirtythreeforty), Andrew King (QuantumEntangledAndy), Daniel Kaiser (presets) and contributors. The protocol framing they travel in is described in
my own [neolink docs](https://github.com/privatecoder/neolink/blob/master/docs/bc-protocol.md). The continuous zoom commands
(`ZoomInc`/`ZoomDec` on the PTZ control message) were found by testing a real camera for this release. See the
[v1.9.15-baichuan.1 notes](https://github.com/privatecoder/go2rtc/releases/tag/v1.9.15-baichuan.1) for the full credits of
the Baichuan source.

## Downloads

Binaries are built by GitHub Actions from this tag for Linux amd64, Linux arm64 and macOS arm64. The Linux files are plain
executables; the macOS one is zipped. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists the checksums.

**Frigate**: save `go2rtc_linux_amd64` (or `_arm64`) as `/config/go2rtc`, make it executable (`chmod 755`) and restart Frigate.

Docker image (linux/amd64, linux/arm64): `ghcr.io/privatecoder/go2rtc:1.9.15-baichuan.2` or `ghcr.io/privatecoder/go2rtc:latest`.
